_comment: The tested versions (ported from ClawDeck's assets/versions.json, same author), the fallback when the signed upscalers.json can't be fetched or verified (mirror.py). Every file is pinned by sha256 and copied to the rolling 'upscalers' release of IHulkSmashI/GameCove-data under an immutable name ("mirror"), so a file moved or replaced upstream never breaks an install; the upstream URL ("url") is the second source, same sha256. .github/workflows/upscalers.yml puts these files on the mirror on its first run and keeps them.

xess_xmx_linux.sha256_note: xess-xmx-linux-20261111.zip (25120081 bytes), downloaded on 2026-11-10; the same file ClawDeck pins at 4cf5cf9. Script changes since 20261104 read before pinning: install.sh picks stock mode on Xe3 (the package's unpatched Mesa 26.3 plus its Vulkan layer, five more session variables that GameCove carries per game like the others) and writes a small session-check copy to ~/.config/xess-xmx; session-check.sh checks the ICD file first and clears old-toolchain kernels; new xmx-stock.sh (the stock-mode launcher). Nothing new downloads, nothing runs as root.
xess_xmx_linux.note: 20261111: Mesa 26.3.0 final; on Xe3 (Claw 8 EX / Panther Lake) install.sh now defaults to stock mode: the package's unpatched Mesa 26.3 plus the Vulkan layer VK_LAYER_XESS_xmx (its session file adds MESA, VK_ADD_LAYER_PATH, VK_LOADER_LAYERS_ENABLE, XMX_LAYER_HELPER, XMX_IGC_DIR, which ClawDeck carries per game like the others and sets before the container, as upstream's xmx-stock.sh does; the layer writes the same anv_canary); Xe2 (Claw 8 AI+) and older stay on the patched driver. XESS=latest also serves D3D11 and Vulkan games. 20261107: hardening of the driver, shim and hook, the other missing kernels compiled in the background on a cache miss, Mesa 26.3 patch 0006 (a Cyberpunk 2077 crash), the session check run from ~/.config/xess-xmx (stock drivers when the package folder is gone), any case of the prefix driver store; the session file, hook mark and shim path ClawDeck reads are unchanged. Also an experimental Vulkan layer for the stock driver (xmx-stock.sh), not used by ClawDeck yet. 20261104: low latency with XeSS frame generation on by default (IGDEXT_XELL_CAP), FSR 3.1+ games on XeSS (FSR=xess), XESS_FG up to 8x
xess_xmx_linux.scripts_note: Every shell script in the tested package (relative to its folder), read from xess-xmx-linux-20261111.zip on 2026-11-10. The helper runs install.sh only when every .sh in the unpacked package matches this list, and the signed index replaces this pin only with a build whose scripts are the same (review 2, problem 8).

reframework.note: Capcom RE Engine games: dinput8.dll (23252480 bytes, REFramework 0.1.0.69) next to the game's exe. onehoon's fork (the fork's author), release 15 built 2026-10-22, whose notes say to use it with OptiScaler in Capcom games: a working Windows Onimusha install runs exactly this file, and it booted and played with optiscaler_v10 on a Claw 8 EX on Bazzite (2026-11-04). Replaces praydog's nightly 01433: ClawDeck installs REFramework only together with the Capcom OptiScaler setup, and the fork is the build that setup was tested with. Release 18 (2026-11-05) since 2026-11-09: three upstream syncs over release 15 (Lua JSON and LooseFileLoader fixes, HookManager error paths and thread safety, ARM64EC hooks skipped), dinput8.dll 23262720 bytes; release 15's dll stays recognised (previous_dll_sha256) so Remove still takes it out.

optiscaler.note: ClawDeck's own OptiScaler (optiscaler.py): the same release and OptiPatcher build Decky Framegen v0.17 pins, with the same sha256.

optiscaler_v10.note: Capcom RE Engine games only (optiscaler.py layout 'subfolder'): OptiScaler.dll as the proxy and OptiScaler.ini next to the exe, everything else in OptiScaler\ (OptiDllPath), OptiPatcher in OptiScaler\plugins. a working Windows Onimusha install uses 0.9.5-pre4, which isn't published on GitHub; this public v10 nightly ran Onimusha with onehoon's REFramework on a Claw 8 EX on Bazzite (2026-11-04). Every other game stays on 'optiscaler' (0.9.4). fakenvapi v1.4.1 (FakeMichau) goes in OptiScaler\ with the tested fakenvapi.ini, as in the tested folder: its fakenvapi.dll (415232 bytes) is byte-identical to the one OptiScaler 0.9.4 ships. OptiScaler v10 has fakenvapi built in ([fakenvapi] UseFakenvapi, set to true) and doesn't load the file; it is there to match the setup tested on the Claw.

fsr4_xmx.note: nitec's FSR 4.1.2 build for the XMX cores (OptiScaler community), the same files the tested setup installs on Intel (its Archives/Custom/FSR4_XMX). Hosted on ClawDeck's fsr4-xmx-files branch, pinned by commit (not on the Releases page); downloaded into ~/fsr4-xmx when missing, each sha256 checked (the maintainer's working copy on the Claw 8 EX, 2026-11-04).

fsr4_amd.license: AMD FidelityFX SDK binary licence (Kits/FidelityFX/docs/license.md): binary redistribution allowed with its notice; shipped unmodified inside every GameCove package with that notice (licenses/AMD-FidelityFX-SDK-license.md), and fetched from AMD's repository when a package has none
fsr4_amd.note: AMD FSR SDK 2.4.0 (2026-10-28): FSR Upscaling 4.1.2, ML model picked by GPU (FP8 RDNA4, INT8 RDNA3/RDNA2 dGPU and Strix Halo, lightweight INT8 for Z2 Extreme / 890M / Z2 A). The same file ClawDeck keeps as fsr-original.dll next to nitec's XMX build. Under Proton FSR 4 needs a Proton with AMD's driver extension shim (Proton-CachyOS, GE-Proton).

lsfg_vk.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (lsfg-vk.dev, 2026-08-27): not part of GameCove's package and not on its mirror; fetched unmodified from its author's own site when the user asks for it
lsfg_vk.note: lsfg-vk 2.0.0 (2026-09-05; 561348 bytes, downloaded 2026-11-10): lib/liblsfg-vk-layer.so, share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d/VkLayer_LSFGVK_frame_generation.json, bin/lsfg-vk-cli. Needs the user's own Lossless Scaling (Steam app 993090, beta branch lsfg-vk).
